title: .NET Framework
summary: The .NET Framework is a proprietary Microsoft software platform that runs primarily on Windows, implementing the Common Language Infrastructure (CLI) standard. It comprises a large class library (FCL) and a runtime environment (CLR) that executes managed code, providing services like memory management, security, and exception handling. While initially closed, Microsoft has issued patent promises and relicensed related runtimes under permissive licenses, though core Framework components remain proprietary.

mechanisms.title: Common Language Runtime (CLR)
mechanisms.explanation: The CLR is an application virtual machine that executes managed code, providing foundational services such as memory management, security, and exception handling. It acts as the execution environment for programs written for the Framework.

mechanisms.title: Framework Class Library (FCL)
mechanisms.explanation: The FCL is a large class library that provides functionality for user interfaces, data access, database connectivity, cryptography, web development, numeric algorithms, and network communications. Programmers combine source code with the FCL to build applications.
